title: A Comprehensive Guide to Vegetable Extract Processing and Extraction Systems by Seppa Solutions
overviewTitle: Overview of Seppa's Vegetable Extract Processing Plant Solutions
overviewsubDescription: When an investor considers entering the processed foods sector, they usually ask: Can a single production line serve more than one product? In the case of vegetable extracts, the answer is clear. These extracts are the foundation on which entire industries are built, from concentrated tomato juices to ready-made sauce bases.

Seppa Solutions relies on multi-stage extraction engineering, combining mechanical grinding, centrifugal separation, and partial vacuum evaporation. The goal of this sequence is to preserve the natural flavor and nutritional value of vegetables, rather than losing them in high-temperature stages as happens in older, conventional systems.

An interesting point here: the sterilization standards we apply in vegetable extraction units are largely inspired by the sterilization protocols approved in liquid dairy product lines, specifically CIP (Clean-in-Place) systems that prevent any bacterial contamination between batches. This similarity is no coincidence; both industries deal with heat-sensitive liquids that spoil quickly if not managed precisely.

In fact, many of the investors we deal with already own an existing production line for processing liquid dairy products, and ask us: Can a vegetable extraction unit be added without destroying the existing structure? The answer in most cases is yes, because many components of existing food production lines, such as chilled storage tanks and distribution piping, are reusable with limited modifications.

contentBlocks.title: Turnkey Vegetable Extract Processing & Line Integration
paragraphs: Seppa Solutions designs and integrates complete processed vegetable lines on a turnkey basis, ensuring that transfer pipelines, steam injection valves, and evaporation systems work cohesively.
Our lines feature advanced thermal protection control systems to avoid overheating sensitive ingredients like carrot juice or beet pulp, retaining color and essential nutrients.
By utilizing unified control architectures (PLC and SCADA), plant operators can switch recipes quickly, adapting the line speed and temperature depending on seasonal crop availability.
Sanitary design is applied throughout the entire layout, utilizing automated CIP washing to guarantee bacterial cleanliness between batches and during product changes.

methodology.title: Seppa's Methodology: From Concept to Production Line
methodology.subtitle: An integrated approach starting with mass balance calculations and ending with commissioning and training.

steps.title: Phase 1: Mass Balance Study
steps.description: Calculate raw material quantities and expected outputs at each stage to size storage tanks and pumping rates accurately.

steps.title: Phase 2: Extraction Unit Design
steps.description: Select the appropriate vegetable extractor and configure the grinding and filtering profile based on vegetable characteristics.

steps.title: Phase 3: Integration & Pipework
steps.description: Physical installation of piping, integrating control networks, and interfacing units with existing dairy or liquid lines.

steps.title: Phase 4: Commissioning & Optimization
steps.description: Monitor temperature, pressure, and viscosity to ensure several consecutive batches meet the agreed parameters.

steps.title: Phase 5: Training & Follow-up Review
steps.description: Provide hands-on training for operators and review line performance after six months to ensure maximum seasonal efficiency.

faqs.question: What quality parameters are essential in a tomato paste factory?
faqs.answer: Brix level, acidity (pH), and final viscosity must be closely controlled, alongside complete package sterilization prior to filling to prevent bacterial contamination.

faqs.question: How is a vegetable extraction machine maintained?
faqs.answer: Routine maintenance includes checking grinding blades, calibrating temperature sensors, and carrying out deep weekly cleaning in addition to daily CIP cycles.

faqs.question: Can vegetable extraction lines be integrated with existing dairy lines?
faqs.answer: Yes, in many cases CIP systems and main utilities can be shared, which significantly lowers initial capital investments.

faqs.question: How long does it take to install a complete ketchup processing line?
faqs.answer: Depending on the scale, it usually takes between three to six months from final contract signing to initial commissioning trials.

faqs.question: Does vegetable processing change significantly depending on the crop?
faqs.answer: Yes, tomatoes require completely different crushing and filtering profiles than carrots or beets. We adjust centrifugal speeds and processing heats accordingly.
